sanskrit: api cātra purāvṛttaṃ kathayiṣyāmi te 'nagha
english: And on this matter I shall recount to you a tale of olden days, O sinless one.

sanskrit: ṛṣīṇām uttamaṃ dhīmān kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaṃ śukaḥ abhivādyāhnikaṃ kṛtvā śuciḥ prayatamānasaḥ pitaraṃ paripapraccha dṛṣṭalokaparāvaram
english: The wise Śuka, having saluted Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana, foremost among the sages, and having performed the daily rites, pure and earnest of mind, questioned his father, who had beheld the higher and lower worlds.

sanskrit: ko yajñaḥ sarvayajñānāṃ variṣṭha upalakṣyate kiṃ ca kṛtvā paraṃ svargaṃ prāpnuvanti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: Which sacrifice is held to be the most excellent of all sacrifices? And by doing what do the wise attain the highest heaven?

sanskrit: kena devāḥ pavitreṇa svargam aśnanti vā vibho kiṃ ca yajñasya yajñatvaṃ kva ca yajñaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: By what purifying thing, O mighty one, do the gods enjoy heaven? And wherein lies the sacrificial essence of a sacrifice, and upon what is sacrifice established?

sanskrit: dānānām uttamaṃ kiṃ ca kiṃ ca satram ataḥ param pavitrāṇāṃ pavitraṃ ca yat tad brūhi mamānagha
english: What is the highest of gifts, and what beyond that is the supreme rite of offering? And what is the purest of pure things — tell me that, O sinless one.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu vacanaṃ vyāsaḥ paramadharmavit putrāyākathayat sarvaṃ tattvena bharatarṣabha
english: Hearing these words, Vyāsa, supreme knower of dharma, told his son all of it truly, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca gāvaḥ pratiṣṭhā bhūtānāṃ tathā gāvaḥ parāyaṇam gāvaḥ puṇyāḥ pavitrāś ca pāvanaṃ dharma eva ca
english: Vyāsa said: The cows are the foundation of all beings, and the cows are their refuge; the cows are holy and pure, the very means of purification and dharma itself.

sanskrit: pūrvam āsannaśṛṅgā vai gāva ity anuśuśrumaḥ śṛṅgārthe samupāsanta tāḥ kila prabhum avyayam
english: In ancient times the cows were hornless, so we have heard; and to gain horns they worshipped the imperishable Lord.

sanskrit: tato brahmā tu gāḥ prāyam upaviṣṭāḥ samīkṣya ha īpsitaṃ pradadau tābhyo gobhyaḥ pratyekaśaḥ prabhuḥ
english: Then Brahmā, beholding the cows seated in fasting devotion, the Lord granted to each of those cows, one by one, the boon they desired.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ śṛṅgāṇy ajāyanta yasyā yādṛṅ manogatam nānāvarṇāḥ śṛṅgavantyas tā vyarocanta putraka
english: Horns arose upon them, for each according to her heart's wish; and bearing horns of varied hues, they shone resplendent, O dear son.

sanskrit: brahmaṇā varadattās tā havyakavyapradāḥ śubhāḥ puṇyāḥ pavitrāḥ subhagā divyasaṃsthānalakṣaṇāḥ gāvas tejo mahad divyaṃ gavāṃ dānaṃ praśasyate
english: Blessed by Brahmā with boons, those auspicious cows became the givers of oblations to gods and ancestors — holy, pure, fortunate, marked with divine form and feature. The cows possess a great and divine splendour, and the gift of cows is extolled.

sanskrit: ye caitāḥ saṃprayacchanti sādhavo vītamatsarāḥ te vai sukṛtinaḥ proktāḥ sarvadānapradāś ca te gavāṃ lokaṃ tathā puṇyam āpnuvanti ca te 'nagha
english: Those righteous men, free of envy, who bestow these cows are called doers of merit and givers of every gift; and they attain the holy world of the cows, O sinless one.

sanskrit: yatra vṛkṣā madhuphalā divyapuṣpaphalopagāḥ puṣpāṇi ca sugandhīni divyāni dvijasattama
english: There the trees bear honeyed fruit and are laden with divine blossoms and fruit, and there are fragrant celestial flowers, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: sarvā maṇimayī bhūmiḥ sūkṣmakāñcanavālukā sarvatra sukhasaṃsparśā niṣpaṅkā nīrajā śubhā
english: The whole ground is wrought of gems, its sand fine gold; everywhere soft to the touch, free of mire, free of dust, and lovely.

sanskrit: raktotpalavanaiś caiva maṇidaṇḍair hiraṇmayaiḥ taruṇādityasaṃkāśair bhānti tatra jalāśayāḥ
english: There the pools shine, set about with groves of red lotuses and with golden, jewel-stemmed stalks, gleaming like the newly-risen sun.

sanskrit: mahārhamaṇipatraiś ca kāñcanaprabhakesaraiḥ nīlotpalavimiśraiś ca sarobhir bahupaṅkajaiḥ
english: And with lakes thick with many lotuses, their leaves of priceless gems, their filaments gleaming like gold, mingled with blue water-lilies.

sanskrit: karavīravanaiḥ phullaiḥ sahasrāvartasaṃvṛtaiḥ saṃtānakavanaiḥ phullair vṛkṣaiś ca samalaṃkṛtāḥ
english: They are adorned with blossoming oleander groves girdled by a thousand eddies, with flowering saṃtānaka groves, and with fair trees.

sanskrit: nirmalābhiś ca muktābhir maṇibhiś ca mahādhanaiḥ uddhūtapulinās tatra jātarūpaiś ca nimnagāḥ
english: And there the rivers cast up sand-banks heaped with spotless pearls, with gems of great worth, and with pure gold.

sanskrit: sarvaratnamayaiś citrair avagāḍhā nagottamaiḥ jātarūpamayaiś cānyair hutāśanasamaprabhaiḥ
english: They are studded with wondrous peaks of every jewel, with lofty mountains, and with others of pure gold radiant as fire.

sanskrit: sauvarṇagirayas tatra maṇiratnaśiloccayāḥ sarvaratnamayair bhānti śṛṅgaiś cārubhir ucchritaiḥ
english: There are golden mountains, masses of rock of gems and jewels, that shine with lovely upraised peaks made of every precious stone.

sanskrit: nityapuṣpaphalās tatra nagāḥ patrarathākulāḥ divyagandharasaiḥ puṣpaiḥ phalaiś ca bharatarṣabha
english: There the trees, ever in flower and fruit, throng with birds, bearing blossoms and fruits of divine fragrance and savour, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: ramante puṇyakarmāṇas tatra nityaṃ yudhiṣṭhira sarvakāmasamṛddhārthā niḥśokā gatamanyavaḥ
english: There the doers of holy deeds disport themselves forever, O Yudhiṣṭhira, every desire fulfilled, free of sorrow, their wrath departed.

sanskrit: vimāneṣu vicitreṣu ramaṇīyeṣu bhārata modante puṇyakarmāṇo viharanto yaśasvinaḥ
english: In gorgeous and delightful aerial cars, O Bhārata, the glorious doers of holy deeds rejoice, roaming at their pleasure.

sanskrit: upakrīḍanti tān rājañ śubhāś cāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ etāṃl lokān avāpnoti gāṃ dattvā vai yudhiṣṭhira
english: And fair throngs of apsarases sport before them, O king. Such worlds does one attain by the gift of a cow, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yāsām adhipatiḥ pūṣā māruto balavān balī aiśvarye varuṇo rājā tā māṃ pāntu yugaṃdharāḥ
english: May those cows, of whom Pūṣan is lord, and the mighty, powerful Wind, and king Varuṇa over their abundance, the bearers of the yoke, protect me.

sanskrit: surūpā bahurūpāś ca viśvarūpāś ca mātaraḥ prājāpatyā iti brahmañ japen nityaṃ yatavrataḥ
english: "The mothers, fair of form, of many forms, of every form, born of Prajāpati" — thus, O brāhmaṇa, let one of disciplined vows recite daily.

sanskrit: gās tu śuśrūṣate yaś ca samanveti ca sarvaśaḥ tasmai tuṣṭāḥ prayacchanti varān api sudurlabhān
english: And to him who serves the cows and waits upon them in every way, they, well pleased, grant boons even hard to obtain.

sanskrit: na druhyen manasā cāpi goṣu tā hi sukhapradāḥ arcayeta sadā caiva namaskāraiś ca pūjayet dāntaḥ prītamanā nityaṃ gavāṃ vyuṣṭiṃ tathāśnute
english: Let one bear no malice toward cows even in thought, for they are the givers of happiness; let one ever revere them and honour them with salutations. Self-controlled and glad of heart, one thus enjoys the rich reward of the cows.

sanskrit: yena devāḥ pavitreṇa bhuñjate lokam uttamam yat pavitraṃ pavitrāṇāṃ tad ghṛtaṃ śirasā vahet
english: That purifier by which the gods enjoy the highest world, the purest of pure things — that clarified butter let one bear upon one's head.

sanskrit: ghṛtena juhuyād agniṃ ghṛtena svasti vācayet ghṛtaṃ prāśed ghṛtaṃ dadyād gavāṃ vyuṣṭiṃ tathāśnute
english: With clarified butter let one offer to the fire, with clarified butter pronounce the blessing; let one taste it and bestow it — thus one enjoys the rich reward of the cows.

sanskrit: tryaham uṣṇaṃ piben mūtraṃ tryaham uṣṇaṃ pibet payaḥ gavām uṣṇaṃ payaḥ pītvā tryaham uṣṇaṃ ghṛtaṃ pibet tryaham uṣṇaṃ ghṛtaṃ pītvā vāyubhakṣo bhavet tryaham
english: For three days let one drink the warm urine of cows, for three days drink their warm milk; having drunk the warm milk for three days, let one drink the warm clarified butter for three days; and having drunk the warm butter for three days, let one live for three days on air alone.

sanskrit: nirhṛtaiś ca yavair gobhir māsaṃ prasṛtayāvakaḥ brahmahatyāsamaṃ pāpaṃ sarvam etena śudhyati
english: And living for a month on a handful of barley-gruel made from barley trodden out by cows, one is cleansed of every sin, even one equal to the slaying of a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: parābhavārthaṃ daityānāṃ devaiḥ śaucam idaṃ kṛtam devatvam api ca prāptāḥ saṃsiddhāś ca mahābalāḥ
english: This rite of purification was performed by the gods for the undoing of the daityas; and thereby the mighty ones attained godhood and were made perfect.

sanskrit: gāvaḥ pavitrāḥ puṇyāś ca pāvanaṃ paramaṃ mahat tāś ca dattvā dvijātibhyo naraḥ svargam upāśnute
english: The cows are pure and holy, the supreme and mighty means of purification; and by bestowing them upon the twice-born, a man attains heaven.

sanskrit: gavāṃ madhye śucir bhūtvā gomatīṃ manasā japet pūtābhir adbhir ācamya śucir bhavati nirmalaḥ
english: Made pure, in the midst of cows let one recite the Gomatī hymn in mind; having sipped purified water, he becomes pure and spotless.

sanskrit: agnimadhye gavāṃ madhye brāhmaṇānāṃ ca saṃsadi vidyāvedavratasnātā brāhmaṇāḥ puṇyakarmiṇaḥ
english: In the midst of the fire, in the midst of cows, and in the assembly of brāhmaṇas — the brāhmaṇas, accomplished in knowledge, the Veda, and vows, doers of holy deeds —

sanskrit: adhyāpayerañ śiṣyān vai gomatīṃ yajñasaṃmitām trirātropoṣitaḥ śrutvā gomatīṃ labhate varam
english: should teach their pupils the Gomatī hymn, deemed equal to a sacrifice. Having fasted for three nights and heard the Gomatī, one obtains a boon.

sanskrit: putrakāmaś ca labhate putraṃ dhanam athāpi ca patikāmā ca bhartāraṃ sarvakāmāṃś ca mānavaḥ gāvas tuṣṭāḥ prayacchanti sevitā vai na saṃśayaḥ
english: He who longs for a son obtains a son, and wealth besides; she who longs for a husband obtains a husband; and a man obtains all his desires. The cows, when served, well pleased, bestow these things — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: evam etā mahābhāgā yajñiyāḥ sarvakāmadāḥ rohiṇya iti jānīhi naitābhyo vidyate param
english: Thus know these glorious ones, fit for sacrifice, granters of every desire, to be the Rohiṇīs; there is nothing higher than they.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa mahātejāḥ śukaḥ pitrā mahātmanā pūjayām āsa gā nityaṃ tasmāt tvam api pūjaya
english: Thus addressed by his great-souled father, Śuka of mighty splendour ever honoured the cows; therefore do you too honour them.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca mayā gavāṃ purīṣaṃ vai śriyā juṣṭam iti śrutam etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ saṃśayo 'tra hi me mahān
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I have heard that the dung of cows is graced by Śrī. This I wish to hear, for herein my doubt is great.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam gobhir nṛpeha saṃvādaṃ śriyā bharatasattama
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recount an ancient tale, O king — a colloquy between the cows and Śrī, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: śrīḥ kṛtveha vapuḥ kāntaṃ gomadhyaṃ praviveśa ha gāvo 'tha vismitās tasyā dṛṣṭvā rūpasya saṃpadam
english: Śrī, having assumed a lovely form, entered into the midst of the cows; and the cows, beholding the perfection of her beauty, were amazed.

sanskrit: gāva ūcuḥ kāsi devi kuto vā tvaṃ rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi vismitāḥ sma mahābhāge tava rūpasya saṃpadā
english: The cows said: Who are you, O goddess, and whence have you come, peerless in beauty upon the earth? We are amazed, O glorious one, at the perfection of your beauty.

sanskrit: icchāmas tvāṃ vayaṃ jñātuṃ kā tvaṃ kva ca gamiṣyasi tattvena ca suvarṇābhe sarvam etad bravīhi naḥ
english: We wish to know you: who are you, and whither will you go? Tell us all this truly, O you of golden lustre.

sanskrit: śrīr uvāca lokakāntāsmi bhadraṃ vaḥ śrīr nāmneha pariśrutā mayā daityāḥ parityaktā vinaṣṭāḥ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ
english: Śrī said: I am the beloved of the worlds, blessings upon you; I am renowned here by the name of Śrī. The daityas, forsaken by me, have perished for everlasting years.

sanskrit: indro vivasvān somaś ca viṣṇur āpo 'gnir eva ca mayābhipannā ṛdhyante ṛṣayo devatās tathā
english: Indra, Vivasvat, Soma, and Viṣṇu, the waters and Agni too, the sages and the gods — all whom I attend upon prosper.

sanskrit: yāṃś ca dviṣāmy ahaṃ gāvas te vinaśyanti sarvaśaḥ dharmārthakāmahīnāś ca te bhavanty asukhānvitāḥ
english: And those whom I hate, O cows, perish utterly; bereft of dharma, wealth, and pleasure, they become beset with misery.

sanskrit: evaṃprabhāvāṃ māṃ gāvo vijānīta sukhapradām icchāmi cāpi yuṣmāsu vastuṃ sarvāsu nityadā āgatā prārthayānāhaṃ śrījuṣṭā bhavatānaghāḥ
english: Know me, O cows, to be of such power, the bestower of happiness; and I desire to dwell within you all forever. I have come beseeching: be graced with Śrī, O sinless ones.

sanskrit: gāva ūcuḥ adhruvāṃ cañcalāṃ ca tvāṃ sāmānyāṃ bahubhiḥ saha na tvām icchāmi bhadraṃ te gamyatāṃ yatra rocate
english: The cows said: You are unsteady and fickle, shared in common with many; we do not desire you. Blessings upon you — go where it pleases you.

sanskrit: vapuṣmantyo vayaṃ sarvāḥ kim asmākaṃ tvayādya vai yatreṣṭaṃ gamyatāṃ tatra kṛtakāryā vayaṃ tvayā
english: We are all comely of body; what need have we of you today? Go wherever you wish; we are well content without you.

sanskrit: śrīr uvāca kim etad vaḥ kṣamaṃ gāvo yan māṃ nehābhyanandatha na māṃ saṃprati gṛhṇītha kasmād vai durlabhāṃ satīm
english: Śrī said: Is this seemly of you, O cows, that you do not welcome me here? Why do you not now receive me, hard to win as I am?

sanskrit: satyaś ca lokavādo 'yaṃ loke carati suvratāḥ svayaṃ prāpte paribhavo bhavatīti viniścayaḥ
english: And there is a true saying current in the world, O you of good vows, which holds for certain: "What comes of itself is held in contempt."

sanskrit: mahad ugraṃ tapaḥ kṛtvā māṃ niṣevanti mānavāḥ devadānavagandharvāḥ piśācoragarākṣasāḥ
english: Having wrought great and fierce austerity, men attend upon me — gods, dānavas, and gandharvas, piśācas, serpents, and rākṣasas.

sanskrit: kṣamam etad dhi vo gāvaḥ pratigṛhṇīta mām iha nāvamanyā hy ahaṃ saumyās trailokye sacarācare
english: It is fitting for you, O cows: receive me here. For I am not to be slighted, O gentle ones, throughout the three worlds with all that moves and is still.

sanskrit: gāva ūcuḥ nāvamanyāmahe devi na tvāṃ paribhavāmahe adhruvā calacittāsi tatas tvāṃ varjayāmahe
english: The cows said: We do not slight you, O goddess, nor do we hold you in contempt; you are unsteady and fickle of mind, and for that reason we shun you.

sanskrit: bahunātra kim uktena gamyatāṃ yatra vāñchasi vapuṣmatyo vayaṃ sarvāḥ kim asmākaṃ tvayānaghe
english: What need of many words here? Go where you will. We are all comely of body; what need have we of you, O sinless one?

sanskrit: śrīr uvāca avajñātā bhaviṣyāmi sarvalokeṣu mānadāḥ pratyākhyānena yuṣmābhiḥ prasādaḥ kriyatām iti
english: Śrī said: I shall be despised in all the worlds, O bestowers of honour, if I am refused by you. Show me your grace.

sanskrit: mahābhāgā bhavatyo vai śaraṇyāḥ śaraṇāgatām paritrāyantu māṃ nityaṃ bhajamānām aninditām mānanāṃ tv aham icchāmi bhavatyaḥ satataṃ śubhāḥ
english: Glorious are you and worthy refuges; deliver me, who have come for shelter, who devote myself to you forever and am blameless. I desire your regard always, O auspicious ones.

sanskrit: apy ekāṅge tu vo vastum icchāmi ca sukutsite na vo 'sti kutsitaṃ kiṃ cid aṅgeṣv ālakṣyate 'naghāḥ
english: I wish to dwell even in some one part of you, however lowly. Yet there is nothing lowly to be seen in your limbs, O sinless ones.

sanskrit: puṇyāḥ pavitrāḥ subhagā mamādeśaṃ prayacchata vaseyaṃ yatra cāṅge 'haṃ tan me vyākhyātum arhatha
english: Holy, pure, and fortunate ones, grant me your bidding; in which part I am to dwell, that you should declare to me.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam uktās tu tā gāvaḥ śubhāḥ karuṇavatsalāḥ saṃmantrya sahitāḥ sarvāḥ śriyam ūcur narādhipa
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed, those auspicious cows, tender with compassion, having taken counsel together, all spoke to Śrī, O lord of men.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ mānanā kāryā tavāsmābhir yaśasvini śakṛnmūtre nivasa naḥ puṇyam etad dhi naḥ śubhe
english: You must surely be honoured by us, O glorious one; dwell within our dung and urine, for this is holy in us, O auspicious one.

sanskrit: śrīr uvāca diṣṭyā prasādo yuṣmābhiḥ kṛto me 'nugrahātmakaḥ evaṃ bhavatu bhadraṃ vaḥ pūjitāsmi sukhapradāḥ
english: Śrī said: Happily have you shown me grace, full of favour. So be it; blessings upon you. I am honoured, O bestowers of happiness.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evaṃ kṛtvā tu samayaṃ śrīr gobhiḥ saha bhārata paśyantīnāṃ tatas tāsāṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Bhīṣma said: Having thus made her compact with the cows, O Bhārata, Śrī vanished then and there, even as they looked on.

sanskrit: etad gośakṛtaḥ putra māhātmyaṃ te 'nuvarṇitam māhātmyaṃ ca gavāṃ bhūyaḥ śrūyatāṃ gadato mama
english: Thus, my son, has the greatness of cow-dung been recounted to you; and now hear further of the greatness of the cows as I tell it.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ye ca gāḥ saṃprayacchanti hutaśiṣṭāśinaś ca ye teṣāṃ satrāṇi yajñāś ca nityam eva yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: Those who bestow cows, and those who eat only what remains after the oblation, possess the merit of sacrificial rites and sacrifices perpetually, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: ṛte dadhighṛteneha na yajñaḥ saṃpravartate tena yajñasya yajñatvam atomūlaṃ ca lakṣyate
english: Without curds and clarified butter no sacrifice can proceed; therein lies the sacrificial essence of a sacrifice, and herein its very root is seen.

sanskrit: dānānām api sarveṣāṃ gavāṃ dānaṃ praśasyate gāvaḥ śreṣṭhāḥ pavitrāś ca pāvanaṃ hy etad uttamam
english: Of all gifts whatsoever, the gift of cows is extolled; the cows are most excellent and pure, and this is the supreme means of purification.

sanskrit: puṣṭyartham etāḥ seveta śāntyartham api caiva ha payo dadhi ghṛtaṃ yāsāṃ sarvapāpapramocanam
english: For prosperity let one serve them, and for peace as well — those whose milk, curds, and clarified butter release one from all sin.

sanskrit: gāvas tejaḥ paraṃ proktam iha loke paratra ca na gobhyaḥ paramaṃ kiṃ cit pavitraṃ puruṣarṣabha
english: The cows are declared the supreme splendour in this world and the next; there is nothing more purifying than cows, O bull among men.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam pitāmahasya saṃvādam indrasya ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: On this too they recount an ancient tale — a colloquy between the Grandsire and Indra, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: parābhūteṣu daityeṣu śakre tribhuvaneśvare prajāḥ samuditāḥ sarvāḥ satyadharmaparāyaṇāḥ
english: When the daityas had been vanquished and Śakra was lord of the three worlds, all creatures throve, devoted to truth and dharma.

sanskrit: atharṣayaḥ sagandharvāḥ kiṃnaroragarākṣasāḥ devāsurasuparṇāś ca prajānāṃ patayas tathā paryupāsanta kauravya kadā cid vai pitāmaham
english: Then the sages with the gandharvas, the kiṃnaras, serpents, and rākṣasas, the gods, asuras, and suparṇas, and the lords of creatures — once upon a time, O Kauravya, they waited upon the Grandsire.

sanskrit: nāradaḥ parvataś caiva viśvāvasuhahāhuhū divyatāneṣu gāyantaḥ paryupāsanta taṃ prabhum
english: Nārada and Parvata, Viśvāvasu, Hāhā, and Hūhū, singing in divine melodies, waited upon that Lord.

sanskrit: tatra divyāni puṣpāṇi prāvahat pavanas tathā ājahrur ṛtavaś cāpi sugandhīni pṛthak pṛthak
english: There the wind wafted celestial flowers, and the seasons too brought fragrant blossoms each in turn.

sanskrit: tasmin devasamāvāye sarvabhūtasamāgame divyavāditrasaṃghuṣṭe divyastrīcāraṇāvṛte indraḥ papraccha deveśam abhivādya praṇamya ca
english: In that gathering of the gods, that assembly of all beings, resounding with celestial instruments and thronged with divine women and cāraṇas, Indra, having saluted and bowed to the Lord of gods, asked him:

sanskrit: devānāṃ bhagavan kasmāl lokeśānāṃ pitāmaha upariṣṭād gavāṃ loka etad icchāmi veditum
english: O blessed Grandsire, wherefore is the world of cows set above that of the gods, the lords of the worlds? This I wish to know.

sanskrit: kiṃ tapo brahmacaryaṃ vā gobhiḥ kṛtam iheśvara devānām upariṣṭād yad vasanty arajasaḥ sukham
english: What austerity or chastity, O Lord, was performed by the cows here, that they dwell in joy, free of passion, above the gods?

sanskrit: tataḥ provāca taṃ brahmā śakraṃ balanisūdanam avajñātās tvayā nityaṃ gāvo balanisūdana
english: Then Brahmā said to Śakra, the slayer of Bala: The cows have ever been slighted by you, O slayer of Bala.
